Grounding: every number traces to a tool result. That includes 15456, 3x5152, 6.13 vs depth, 1-3 ticks below the bid (10002/10002/10000 against bids of 10003/10004/10003), the 772 SELL at 10006, the 13:35:36.550 fill, the 13:35:37.550 cancels and kill switch, price_move 0, reversion 0, otr 7, cancel_ratio 0.95, the 16 s median latency and ~10x the typical size of 500. No numbers are invented.

Consistency: CLOSE_FP rests on one supported explanation, the risk-system cancellation. The kill switch was recorded in the same millisecond, all resting orders were pulled, and there was no favourable move or reversion. That fits the closure standard. The report also flags the residual concerns (one-sided stack, size, resting time) for Level 2.

Weaknesses:
1. Indicator vocabulary. 'Opposite-side execution before the cancel' is listed as NOT matched, but the tape shows one 1000 ms before the cancels. The indicator was present; only the benefit was absent. Cancel timing (1 s after the opposite fill) is never named as an indicator, though it is the classic signal here.
2. Explanations are 'ruled out' by citing evidence IDs, and some cited facts do not support the verdict:
   - Iceberg is ruled out by E4, which does not contain the order types (LIMIT:4 is never cited).
   - Fat finger is ruled out by E2 (the cancel timing) rather than by three separate orders submitted 5 s apart.
   - Stop-out is marked 'undetermined' yet lists ruled_out_by E3.
   - It is not discussed whether the risk cut explains the purpose of the resting orders (feature a), not just their cancellation.
3. The summary omits the submission times, so the reviewer has to reconstruct part of the sequence.

The disposition follows and is grounded, but two or more points (vocabulary and explanation rulings) are weak.
